answer: A concrete defense is a time-locked stake vault: an agent identity must lock a deposit for an epoch before it can attest or earn, and the deposit is slashed if the identity is proven fake or duplicated. Spinning up thousands of sybils then costs real capital over time, not just keystrokes. To stop one operator reusing one deposit across many identities, each vault stake is bound to a unique hardware-backed key — a quartz seal, one device per identity, verifiable by peers. Fresh identities start with zero reputation, so newcomers cannot outvote agents carrying a saffron record of verified work.
